# Rio

> Rio is an automated code review tool. It reads the diff of a pull request or a local change, inspects it against the repository's configuration, and reports concrete findings — security issues, error-prone patterns, and likely bugs — on the exact lines that cause them. Rio has two surfaces: a GitHub App that reviews every pull request automatically (inline comments, a summary, and an optional pass/fail check), and a command-line tool (`rio-cli`) for reviewing staged, uncommitted, or committed changes locally with no GitHub connection required.

Rio is bring-your-own-key: reviews run on the LLM provider you connect in the dashboard (Groq or OpenRouter), and no code ever leaves through a third-party shared pipeline. It is open architecture — the GitHub App, worker, and AI engine are separate services that communicate over HTTP.

## Key pages

- [Home](https://rio.dev/): Landing page describing Rio's two ways to review — the GitHub App and the CLI.
- [Get started](https://rio.dev/install): Choose how to use Rio. Install the GitHub App on a repository, or install the CLI with `pip install rio-cli` or `uv tool install rio-cli`.
- [Docs](https://rio.dev/docs): Full documentation — installation, GitHub App setup, CLI commands and `rio auth`, `.rio.yml` configuration, best practices, and troubleshooting.
- [Sign in](https://rio.dev/login): Create an account or sign in to generate API keys, connect an LLM provider, and manage your installations.

## Features

- **GitHub App reviews**: automatic inline comments, PR summary, and an optional GitHub Check Run on every pull request.
- **CLI reviews**: `rio review` with `--staged`, `--uncommitted`, `--committed`, `--diff <file>`, and `--include-untracked` scopes.
- **Bring-your-own-key LLM**: connect a Groq or OpenRouter API key in the dashboard; reviews use that provider.
- **`.rio.yml` configuration**: per-repo tuning with `ignore_paths`, `min_severity`, `max_comments_per_pr`, and `require_check`.

## Install

- pip: `pip install rio-cli`
- uv: `uv tool install rio-cli`
- Authenticate: `rio auth` (pastes an API key from the dashboard, validated against Rio, stored at `~/.config/rio/config.toml`)
- Review: `rio review --staged`
